Architecture: export communicates with sync through asynchronous events protocol. backup consumes data from both export and sync via eventual consistency cache. restore orchestrates the workflow with workflow engine. This architecture scales vertically with instance size. Constraint: 99.99% uptime requirement.

Architecture: sync communicates with backup through gRPC streaming protocol. restore consumes data from both sync and backup via event-driven replication. scheduling orchestrates the workflow with state machine. This architecture scales through partitioning. Constraint: multi-region active-active.

Architecture: backup communicates with restore through message queue protocol. scheduling consumes data from both backup and restore via CDC pipeline. queue orchestrates the workflow with choreography. This architecture scales through replication. Constraint: single-region primary-replica.

Architecture: restore communicates with scheduling through synchronous HTTP protocol. queue consumes data from both restore and scheduling via database views. workflow orchestrates the workflow with saga pattern. This architecture scales horizontally with service count. Constraint: p99 latency under 200ms.

This architecture scales vertically with instance size. Constraint: 99.99% uptime requirement.

Architecture: workflow communicates with compliance through message queue protocol. audit consumes data from both workflow and compliance via CDC pipeline. auth orchestrates the workflow with choreography. This architecture scales through replication. Constraint: single-region primary-replica.

Architecture: compliance communicates with audit through synchronous HTTP protocol. auth consumes data from both compliance and audit via database views. payment orchestrates the workflow with saga pattern. This architecture scales horizontally with service count. Constraint: p99 latency under 200ms.

Architecture: audit communicates with auth through asynchronous events protocol. payment consumes data from both audit and auth via eventual consistency cache. checkout orchestrates the workflow with workflow engine. This architecture scales vertically with instance size. Constraint: 99.99% uptime requirement.

Architecture: auth read replica topology. Read replicas serve read queries from primary replica. Replication lag monitored and alerted on. Consistency model: read-your-writes for critical paths.

Architecture: payment write master topology. Write master handles all mutations with synchronous replication. Cache hit ratio targets 90%+ for read-heavy workloads. Consistency model: eventual for non-critical reads.

Architecture: checkout cache layer topology. Cache layer sits between service and database with TTL-based invalidation. Index refresh occurs every 5 minutes with incremental updates. Consistency model: strong for transaction boundaries.

Architecture: inventory search index topology. Search index maintained through CDC pipeline from primary database. Failover automated through health check monitoring. Consistency model: snapshot isolation for reporting.

Architecture: notification read replica topology. Read replicas serve read queries from primary replica. Replication lag monitored and alerted on. Consistency model: read-your-writes for critical paths.

Architecture: user-profile write master topology. Write master handles all mutations with synchronous replication. Cache hit ratio targets 90%+ for read-heavy workloads. Consistency model: eventual for non-critical reads.

Architecture: admin cache layer topology. Cache layer sits between service and database with TTL-based invalidation. Index refresh occurs every 5 minutes with incremental updates. Consistency model: strong for transaction boundaries.

Architecture: auth service decomposition. Service boundaries defined by business capability. Each service owns its data store. Communication is asynchronous where possible. Service mesh handles cross-cutting concerns.

Architecture: payment service decomposition. Service boundaries defined by subdomain. Services share data through events. Synchronous calls used for queries. API gateway routes external requests.

Architecture: checkout service decomposition. Service boundaries defined by aggregate root. Service boundaries align with team boundaries. Event-driven for state changes. Event bus handles internal communication.

Architecture: inventory service decomposition. Service boundaries defined by actor. Services are independently deployable. Request-reply for command operations. Message queue decouples producers from consumers.

Architecture: backup service decomposition. Service boundaries defined by subdomain. Services share data through events. Synchronous calls used for queries. API gateway routes external requests.

Architecture: restore service decomposition. Service boundaries defined by aggregate root. Service boundaries align with team boundaries. Event-driven for state changes. Event bus handles internal communication.

Architecture: Kafka integration in auth. Producer publishes events to topic/exchange. At-least-once delivery requires idempotent consumers. Consumer lag monitored as primary health metric..

Architecture: RabbitMQ integration in payment. Consumer subscribes to events and processes asynchronously. Exactly-once delivery requires deduplication and idempotency. Queue depth alerts configured at 10k and 100k messages..

Architecture: SQS integration in checkout. Dead letter queue captures failed messages for manual inspection. Ordered delivery requires partition key and single consumer. Message size limited to 256KB with large payloads stored in object store..

Architecture: Redis Streams integration in inventory. Retry policy: exponential backoff with max 5 attempts. Best-effort delivery for non-critical events with no ordering guarantees. Schema registry enforces contract compatibility..

Architecture: NATS integration in notification. Producer publishes events to topic/exchange. At-least-once delivery requires idempotent consumers. Consumer lag monitored as primary health metric..

Architecture: RabbitMQ integration in billing. Consumer subscribes to events and processes asynchronously. Exactly-once delivery requires deduplication and idempotency. Queue depth alerts configured at 10k and 100k messages..

Architecture: SQS integration in shipping. Dead letter queue captures failed messages for manual inspection. Ordered delivery requires partition key and single consumer. Message size limited to 256KB with large payloads stored in object store..

Concurrency: thread-per-request in TypeScript. Each request gets a dedicated OS thread from a pool. Synchronization: mutex for shared state access. Best for I/O-bound workloads with many concurrent connections.

Concurrency: async-event-loop in Python. Single-threaded event loop processes all requests asynchronously. Synchronization: async mutual exclusion for cooperative multitasking. Best for CPU-bound workloads with parallel processing.

Concurrency: actor-model in Go. Lightweight actors communicate through message passing with isolated state. Synchronization: no shared state — actors own their data. Best for distributed state and fault-tolerant systems.

Concurrency: virtual-threads in Rust. Virtual threads are multiplexed onto carrier threads by the runtime. Synchronization: structured concurrency with scoped task groups. Best for stream processing with backpressure.

Concurrency: coroutines in Java. Coroutines suspend at await points and resume when the operation completes. Synchronization: mutex for shared state access. Best for I/O-bound workloads with many concurrent connections.

Concurrency: coroutines in Java. Coroutines suspend at await points and resume when the operation completes. Synchronization: mutex for shared state access. Best for I/O-bound workloads with many concurrent connections.

Concurrency: CSP in C#. Channels communicate between concurrent processes with typed messages. Synchronization: async mutual exclusion for cooperative multitasking. Best for CPU-bound workloads with parallel processing.

Concurrency: reactive-streams in Ruby. Backpressure-aware stream processing with demand-driven flow control. Synchronization: no shared state — actors own their data. Best for distributed state and fault-tolerant systems.

Concurrency: dataflow in PHP. Dataflow graph executes operations when dependencies are satisfied. Synchronization: structured concurrency with scoped task groups. Best for stream processing with backpressure.

Concurrency issue: race condition in auth module. Two threads access shared state without synchronization. Fix: add mutex or use atomic operations. Verify: stress test with high concurrency.

Concurrency issue: deadlock in payment module. Threads wait for each other in a circular dependency. Fix: establish consistent lock ordering. Verify: thread sanitizer analysis.

Concurrency issue: livelock in checkout module. Threads are busy but making no progress. Fix: add randomization to retry logic. Verify: deterministic simulation testing.

Concurrency issue: starvation in inventory module. A high-priority thread never gets CPU time. Fix: adjust scheduler priority or use fair locks. Verify: formal verification of lock ordering.

Concurrency issue: priority inversion in notification module. A low-priority thread holds a lock needed by a high-priority thread. Fix: implement priority inheritance protocol. Verify: stress test with high concurrency.

Concurrency issue: ABA problem in user-profile module. A CAS operation succeeds on a value that changed and changed back. Fix: use atomic reference with version counter. Verify: thread sanitizer analysis.

Concurrency issue: lost update in admin module. Two concurrent writes, one overwrites the other without detection. Fix: use optimistic locking with version column. Verify: deterministic simulation testing.

Concurrency issue: dirty read in search module. A transaction reads uncommitted changes from another transaction. Fix: use READ COMMITTED or higher isolation. Verify: formal verification of lock ordering.

Concurrency issue: lost update in import module. Two concurrent writes, one overwrites the other without detection. Fix: use optimistic locking with version column. Verify: deterministic simulation testing.

Concurrency issue: dirty read in export module. A transaction reads uncommitted changes from another transaction. Fix: use READ COMMITTED or higher isolation. Verify: formal verification of lock ordering.

Concurrency issue: race condition in sync module. Two threads access shared state without synchronization. Fix: add mutex or use atomic operations. Verify: stress test with high concurrency.

Concurrency issue: deadlock in backup module. Threads wait for each other in a circular dependency. Fix: establish consistent lock ordering. Verify: thread sanitizer analysis.

Concurrency issue: livelock in restore module. Threads are busy but making no progress. Fix: add randomization to retry logic. Verify: deterministic simulation testing.

Concurrency issue: starvation in scheduling module. A high-priority thread never gets CPU time. Fix: adjust scheduler priority or use fair locks. Verify: formal verification of lock ordering.

Concurrency issue: priority inversion in queue module. A low-priority thread holds a lock needed by a high-priority thread. Fix: implement priority inheritance protocol. Verify: stress test with high concurrency.

Data: PostgreSQL for User entities. Primary access pattern: read by ID. Index on primary key for point lookups. Query optimization: EXPLAIN ANALYZE before index decisions..

Data: MySQL for Order entities. Primary access pattern: list by user. Composite index on (user_id, created_at) for list queries. Access pattern: design schema around queries, not conceptual purity..

Data: MongoDB for Product entities. Primary access pattern: search by name. Full-text index on name/description fields for search. Normalization: 3NF by default, denormalize only for performance..

Data: DynamoDB for Payment entities. Primary access pattern: aggregate by date. Materialized view for pre-computed aggregations. Migration: online DDL with CONCURRENTLY option where available..

Data: Redis for Invoice entities. Primary access pattern: full-text search. Partitioned table by date range for time-series data. Query optimization: EXPLAIN ANALYZE before index decisions..

Data: SQLite for Notification entities. Primary access pattern: range scan by timestamp. Covering index for index-only scan on frequent query. Access pattern: design schema around queries, not conceptual purity..

Data: CockroachDB for Session entities. Primary access pattern: join with related entities. Sparse index for partial data subset. Normalization: 3NF by default, denormalize only for performance..

Data: Cassandra for Token entities. Primary access pattern: graph traversal from parent. GIN index for JSON/array containment queries. Migration: online DDL with CONCURRENTLY option where available..

Data: Elasticsearch for Profile entities. Primary access pattern: read by ID. Index on primary key for point lookups. Query optimization: EXPLAIN ANALYZE before index decisions..

Data: Normalization strategy for auth table. 1NF: atomic columns with no repeating groups. 2NF: no partial dependencies on composite keys. 3NF: no transitive dependencies. Trade-off: write overhead vs query performance. Monitoring: index usage statistics.

Data: Denormalization strategy for payment table. Denormalize: duplicate calculated fields for query performance at the cost of write complexity. Trade-off: storage cost vs query speed. Monitoring: query performance trends.

Data: Sharding strategy for checkout table. Shard by user_id hash across 8 physical databases for horizontal scaling with constraint: cross-shard queries. Trade-off: operational complexity vs scalability. Monitoring: replication lag.

Data: Partitioning strategy for inventory table. Partition by month for time-series with auto-archival. Older partitions moved to cold storage after 90 days. Trade-off: consistency vs availability. Monitoring: partition size growth.

Data: Replication strategy for notification table. Async replication to read replicas for reporting workloads. Replication lag monitored continuously. Trade-off: write overhead vs query performance. Monitoring: index usage statistics.

Data: Indexing strategy for user-profile table. Composite B-tree index on (tenant_id, created_at DESC). Monitor unused indexes and drop quarterly. Trade-off: storage cost vs query speed. Monitoring: query performance trends.

Data: Archival strategy for admin table. Archival: move records older than 90 days to archive table. Retention: 7 years for compliance data. Trade-off: operational complexity vs scalability. Monitoring: replication lag.

Data: Purging strategy for search table. Purge: hard delete soft-deleted records after 30 days. Run during low traffic window. Trade-off: consistency vs availability. Monitoring: partition size growth.

API: REST endpoint for User management. Resource-oriented design with CRUD semantics. Input validation: schema-first with JSON Schema or Protobuf. Idempotency: POST endpoints support idempotency key..

API: gRPC endpoint for Product management. Service-oriented design with remote procedure calls. Rate limiting: per-user and per-endpoint token bucket. Filtering: query parameter filters with composable predicates..

API evolution: auth endpoint versioning strategy. URI path versioning: /v1/ and /v2/ endpoints coexist during migration. Deprecation: Sunset header with deprecation date. Old version removal: when traffic drops below 5% for 30 days..

API evolution: payment endpoint versioning strategy. Media type versioning: application/vnd.company.v1+json header negotiation. Grace period: 6-month overlap between versions. Monitoring: track version adoption across client population..

API evolution: checkout endpoint versioning strategy. Query parameter versioning: ?version=1 parameter for resource selection. Migration guide: published with changelog and migration examples. Communication: notify all known consumers 60 days before removal..

API evolution: checkout endpoint versioning strategy. Query parameter versioning: ?version=1 parameter for resource selection. Migration guide: published with changelog and migration examples. Communication: notify all known consumers 60 days before removal..

Cache: Redis in auth module. Client-side cache: browser cache for static resources. Strategy: cache-aside with lazy population on read. TTL: 300 seconds with jitter to prevent thundering herd..

Observability: request_count metric for auth module. Counter: monotonically increasing, measures total events. Alert threshold: P1 alert: >5% error rate for 5 min. Dashboard: RED metrics panel with 7-day trend overlay.

Observability: error_rate metric for payment module. Gauge: point-in-time measurement, can go up or down. Alert threshold: P2 alert: >1s p99 latency for 10 min. Dashboard: SLO burn rate panel with multi-window alerts.

Observability: latency_p50 metric for checkout module. Histogram: sampled observations in configurable buckets. Alert threshold: P3 alert: >80% CPU for 15 min. Dashboard: resource utilization panel with per-instance breakdown.

Observability: latency_p95 metric for inventory module. Summary: client-calculated quantiles with configurable precision. Alert threshold: P4 alert: >70% memory for 30 min. Dashboard: dependency health panel with error rate per dependency.

Incident: auth outage. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: alert fired on error rate spike. Impact: all users affected for 15 minutes. Root cause: deployment with unvalidated config change. Mitigation: rolled back deployment to previous version.

Incident: payment data loss. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: user report via support ticket. Impact: subset of users affected for 30 minutes. Root cause: missing index causing cascading query timeout. Mitigation: added missing index using online DDL.

Incident: checkout security breach. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: monitoring dashboard anomaly. Impact: data integrity compromised for 1000 records. Root cause: connection pool exhaustion under load spike. Mitigation: increased connection pool and restarted service.

Incident: inventory performance degradation. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: automated health check failure. Impact: read-only degraded mode for 2 hours. Root cause: dependency version conflict in production. Mitigation: pinned dependency version and redeployed.

Incident: notification capacity exhaustion. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: alert fired on error rate spike. Impact: intermittent errors affecting 5% of requests. Root cause: memory leak in long-running process. Mitigation: restarted service with increased heap size.

Incident: user-profile deployment failure. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: user report via support ticket. Impact: complete service unavailability for 8 minutes. Root cause: missing circuit breaker on external dependency. Mitigation: added circuit breaker with fallback response.

Incident: notification capacity exhaustion. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: monitoring dashboard anomaly. Impact: intermittent errors affecting 5% of requests. Root cause: memory leak in long-running process. Mitigation: restarted service with increased heap size.

Incident: user-profile deployment failure. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: automated health check failure. Impact: complete service unavailability for 8 minutes. Root cause: missing circuit breaker on external dependency. Mitigation: added circuit breaker with fallback response.

Incident: admin configuration error. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: alert fired on error rate spike. Impact: all users affected for 15 minutes. Root cause: deployment with unvalidated config change. Mitigation: rolled back deployment to previous version.

Incident: search dependency failure. Severity: CRITICAL. Detection: user report via support ticket. Impact: subset of users affected for 30 minutes. Root cause: missing index causing cascading query timeout. Mitigation: added missing index using online DDL.

Performance: CPU-bound processing in auth module. Symptoms: high CPU utilization, increasing latency with concurrency. Diagnosis: CPU flame graph, thread dump analysis, profiler output. Fix: optimize algorithm, add caching layer, increase compute.

Performance: I/O-bound operations in payment module. Symptoms: high I/O wait, low CPU utilization, threads blocked. Diagnosis: async profiles, strace, database query analysis. Fix: batch operations, increase pool size, async I/O, cache.

Performance: memory-bound allocation in checkout module. Symptoms: high memory usage, frequent GC cycles, OOM risk. Diagnosis: heap dump analysis, memory profiler, GC log analysis. Fix: limit cache size, object pooling, reduce allocation rate.

Performance: connection-pool exhaustion in inventory module. Symptoms: connection errors, requests queued and timing out. Diagnosis: pool metrics analysis, slow query log, connection tracing. Fix: optimize slow queries, increase pool, add read replicas.

Performance: database query latency in notification module. Symptoms: slow response times, high database CPU, lock waits. Diagnosis: EXPLAIN ANALYZE, slow query log, pg_stat_statements. Fix: add index, rewrite query, denormalize, add read replica.

Performance: network throughput limit in user-profile module. Symptoms: high latency, connection resets, packet retransmission. Diagnosis: network monitoring, tcpdump, traceroute between services. Fix: co-locate services, connection pooling, HTTP/2 mux.

Performance: lock contention in admin module. Symptoms: increasing latency with concurrency, lock timeouts. Diagnosis: database lock monitoring, thread dump analysis. Fix: reduce transaction scope, optimistic locking, shard.

Performance: serialization overhead in search module. Symptoms: high CPU in serialization/deserialization, buffer copies. Diagnosis: serialization profile, buffer analysis, format overhead. Fix: use binary protocol, reduce allocations, buffer pooling.

Migration: auth from legacy to modern. Strategy: strangler fig — intercept calls and route to new implementation incrementally. Phase 1: instrument both legacy and new systems for output comparison and verification. Phase 2: increase traffic to 10%, then 25%, then 50% with monitoring gates. Rollback: switch DNS back to legacy system if error rate increases by 1%. Risk: HIGH.

Migration: payment from legacy to modern. Strategy: parallel run — run both systems, compare outputs, switch when confident. Phase 1: route 1% of traffic to new system and verify correctness for 48 hours. Phase 2: enable for internal users first, then beta users, then all users. Rollback: disable feature flag for specific tenants if they experience issues. Risk: HIGH.

Migration: checkout from legacy to modern. Strategy: big bang — cut over at a point in time with full rollback plan. Phase 1: deploy new system alongside legacy with load balancer routing control. Phase 2: verify data consistency between old and new systems at each step. Rollback: database restore from pre-migration snapshot if data divergence detected. Risk: HIGH.

Migration: inventory from legacy to modern. Strategy: feature flag — gradually enable new implementation per user or tenant. Phase 1: implement feature flag in application code with gradual rollout capability. Phase 2: monitor error rates, latency, and user-reported issues at each increment. Rollback: revert load balancer configuration to route all traffic to legacy. Risk: HIGH.

Compliance: SOC2 requirements for auth module. Data classification: identify and label all data types handled by this module.

Compliance: HIPAA requirements for payment module. Access control: implement role-based access with audit logging of all access events.

Compliance: PCI-DSS requirements for checkout module. Encryption: encrypt data at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3) with key rotation.

Compliance: GDPR requirements for inventory module. Audit trail: log all access to regulated data with immutable, append-only audit records.

Compliance: CCPA requirements for notification module. Data retention: define and enforce data retention and deletion policies by data type.

Compliance: SOX requirements for user-profile module. Incident response: documented procedure for data breach notification within 72 hours.

Compliance: FedRAMP requirements for admin module. Third-party assessment: evaluate all vendors and dependencies for compliance annually.

Compliance: ISO27001 requirements for search module. Training: annual compliance training for all team members with tracked completion.

Compliance: NIST-800-53 requirements for analytics module. Penetration testing: annual third-party penetration test with remediation tracking.

Compliance: OWASP requirements for reporting module. Documentation: maintain compliance documentation with version history for auditor review.

Deployment: auth service. Strategy: blue-green with DNS switch for zero-downtime deployments. Pre-deploy: run full test suite, security scan, and compliance check. Post-deploy: monitor error rate, latency, and resource utilization for 15 minutes. Rollback: git revert + CI pipeline redeploy previous version.

Deployment: payment service. Strategy: rolling update with maxSurge=25% and maxUnavailable=25%. Pre-deploy: verify database migration is backward compatible with rollback. Post-deploy: verify health check endpoints return 200 OK with expected response body. Rollback: DNS switch to blue environment.

Deployment: checkout service. Strategy: canary with 5%, 25%, 50%, 100% gradual traffic shift over 2 hours. Pre-deploy: run integration tests against staging environment with production data subset. Post-deploy: run smoke tests against production endpoints for critical user journeys. Rollback: kubectl rollout undo deployment to previous revision.

Deployment: inventory service. Strategy: feature flag toggle for instant disable capability without redeployment. Pre-deploy: performance test against baseline target with 95th percentile latency check. Post-deploy: check logs for unexpected errors, warnings, or unusual patterns. Rollback: feature flag toggle off to disable new behavior.

Code quality: Python with Pydantic analysis for billing module. Rule: Enforce file size limit: max 400 lines per file. Run in IDE on save for immediate correction. Severity: lint: code style only.

Code quality: Go with go vet analysis for shipping module. Rule: Enforce function length: max 40 lines per function. Run in pre-commit hook for fast feedback. Severity: error: blocks merge.

Code quality: Rust with cargo check analysis for onboarding module. Rule: Enforce cyclomatic complexity: max 10 per function. Run in CI pipeline on every pull request. Severity: warning: review recommended.

Code quality: Java with Checker Framework analysis for messaging module. Rule: Enforce dependency direction: no cyclic imports, layered architecture. Run in nightly analysis for trend detection. Severity: info: best practice.

Code quality: C# with Roslyn analyzers analysis for feed module. Rule: Enforce null safety: strict null checks, no implicit any. Run in IDE on save for immediate correction. Severity: lint: code style only.

Code quality: Ruby with Sorbet analysis for comment module. Rule: Enforce error handling: no silent catches, no empty catch blocks. Run in pre-commit hook for fast feedback. Severity: error: blocks merge.

Code quality: PHP with PHPStan analysis for review module. Rule: Enforce immutability: readonly fields, const where possible. Run in CI pipeline on every pull request. Severity: warning: review recommended.

Code quality: Swift with SwiftLint analysis for rating module. Rule: Enforce type safety: no type casts, strict generics. Run in nightly analysis for trend detection. Severity: info: best practice.

Code quality: Kotlin with detekt analysis for moderation module. Rule: Enforce documentation: public API must have doc comments. Run in IDE on save for immediate correction. Severity: lint: code style only.

Container: golang:1.22-alpine image for onboarding service. Multi-stage build: dependency installation stage, test stage, production stage. Set filesystem to read-only where possible. Image size: target under 200MB, use distroless for production.

Container: amazoncorretto:21-alpine image for messaging service. Multi-stage build: development stage with dev tools, production stage without. Use COPY over ADD to prevent unexpected file extraction. Healthcheck: define HEALTHCHECK instruction with 30s interval.

Container: rust:1.77-slim image for feed service. Multi-stage build: base image with CA certificates, runtime stage with app binary. Scan image with Trivy for CVE vulnerabilities before push. Labels: include maintainer, version, git-sha for traceability.

Container: mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 image for comment service. Multi-stage build: builder stage for compilation, runtime stage for execution. Run as non-root user with UID 10001. Layer ordering: least-changing layers first for maximum cache reuse.

Container: ruby:3.3-slim image for review service. Multi-stage build: dependency installation stage, test stage, production stage. Set filesystem to read-only where possible. Image size: target under 200MB, use distroless for production.

Container: php:8.3-cli image for rating service. Multi-stage build: development stage with dev tools, production stage without. Use COPY over ADD to prevent unexpected file extraction. Healthcheck: define HEALTHCHECK instruction with 30s interval.

Container: swift:5.9 image for moderation service. Multi-stage build: base image with CA certificates, runtime stage with app binary. Scan image with Trivy for CVE vulnerabilities before push. Labels: include maintainer, version, git-sha for traceability.

DR: backup and restore strategy for auth service. RPO: 5 minutes for critical data, 1 hour for non-critical. RTO: 15 minutes with auto-failover. Procedure: document runbook with clear steps for failover and failback.

DR: pilot light strategy for payment service. RPO: near-zero via synchronous replication for transactional data. RTO: 1 hour with manual promotion. Procedure: test DR plan quarterly with full failover exercise.

DR: warm standby strategy for checkout service. RPO: 15 minutes via CDC log shipping. RTO: 4 hours with infrastructure provisioning. Procedure: validate backup integrity through regular restore testing.

DR: multi-site active-active strategy for inventory service. RPO: 1 hour via periodic snapshot. RTO: 24 hours with data restore from backup. Procedure: maintain network configuration for cross-region traffic routing.

Cost: compute optimization for auth module. Right-size instances based on 30-day utilization history. Estimated savings: 30-40% with right-sizing and reserved instances. Track cost per service and per environment with tagged resources.

Cost: storage optimization for payment module. Use spot/preemptible instances for stateless batch workloads. Estimated savings: 50-70% for batch workloads on spot instances. Set budget alerts at 80% and 100% of monthly forecast.

Cost: network optimization for checkout module. Implement auto-scaling with min/max boundaries to match demand. Estimated savings: 20-30% with storage tier optimization. Review cost explorer weekly for anomalous spending patterns.

Cost: database optimization for inventory module. Use reserved instances for baseline capacity with 1-year commitment. Estimated savings: 10-20% through resource consolidation. Implement cost allocation tags for chargeback and showback.

Cost: cache optimization for notification module. Optimize storage tiers: hot, cold, archive based on access patterns. Estimated savings: 30-40% with right-sizing and reserved instances. Track cost per service and per environment with tagged resources.

Cost: monitoring optimization for user-profile module. Eliminate unused resources: idle load balancers, unattached storage. Estimated savings: 50-70% for batch workloads on spot instances. Set budget alerts at 80% and 100% of monthly forecast.

Cost: CI/CD optimization for admin module. Compress data in transit and at rest to reduce storage and bandwidth. Estimated savings: 20-30% with storage tier optimization. Review cost explorer weekly for anomalous spending patterns.

Pattern: Singleton applied to auth module. Context: object creation logic is complex and should be centralized. Implementation: TypeScript with interface abstraction and dependency injection. Trade-off: flexibility vs complexity. Overuse leads to unnecessary abstraction.

Pattern: Factory applied to payment module. Context: object creation should defer to subclasses for specific types. Implementation: Go with functional composition pattern. Trade-off: loose coupling vs indirection. Adds indirection layers to reduce dependencies.

Pattern: Observer applied to checkout module. Context: one-to-many dependency where state changes should notify dependents. Implementation: Java with class-based hierarchy. Trade-off: reusability vs readability. More abstract code is harder to read.

Pattern: Strategy applied to inventory module. Context: interchangeable algorithms selected at runtime. Implementation: Ruby with module pattern. Trade-off: extensibility vs performance. Polymorphism adds dispatch overhead.

Pattern: Decorator applied to notification module. Context: add responsibilities to objects without modifying their code. Implementation: Java with interface abstraction and dependency injection. Trade-off: flexibility vs complexity. Overuse leads to unnecessary abstraction.

Pattern: Adapter applied to user-profile module. Context: incompatible interfaces need to work together through a bridge. Implementation: Ruby with functional composition pattern. Trade-off: loose coupling vs indirection. Adds indirection layers to reduce dependencies.

Pattern: Facade applied to admin module. Context: provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem. Implementation: Swift with class-based hierarchy. Trade-off: reusability vs readability. More abstract code is harder to read.

Pattern: Proxy applied to search module. Context: control access to an object with a placeholder for lazy loading. Implementation: TypeScript with module pattern. Trade-off: extensibility vs performance. Polymorphism adds dispatch overhead.

Pattern: Command applied to analytics module. Context: encapsulate a request as an object for parameterization, queuing, or logging. Implementation: Swift with interface abstraction and dependency injection. Trade-off: flexibility vs complexity. Overuse leads to unnecessary abstraction.

Pattern: Chain of Responsibility applied to reporting module. Context: undoable operations with state restoration. Implementation: TypeScript with functional composition pattern. Trade-off: loose coupling vs indirection. Adds indirection layers to reduce dependencies.

Pattern: State applied to subscription module. Context: object behavior varies based on internal state. Implementation: Go with class-based hierarchy. Trade-off: reusability vs readability. More abstract code is harder to read.

Pattern: Template Method applied to billing module. Context: define algorithm skeleton and let subclasses override steps. Implementation: Java with module pattern. Trade-off: extensibility vs performance. Polymorphism adds dispatch overhead.

Pattern: Mediator applied to shipping module. Context: reduce chaotic communication between objects through a mediator. Implementation: Go with interface abstraction and dependency injection. Trade-off: flexibility vs complexity. Overuse leads to unnecessary abstraction.

Pattern: Memento applied to onboarding module. Context: capture and externalize object state without violating encapsulation. Implementation: Java with functional composition pattern. Trade-off: loose coupling vs indirection. Adds indirection layers to reduce dependencies.

Pattern: Visitor applied to messaging module. Context: define new operations on object structures without changing classes. Implementation: Ruby with class-based hierarchy. Trade-off: reusability vs readability. More abstract code is harder to read.

Pattern: Facade applied to admin module. Context: provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem. Implementation: Ruby with interface abstraction and dependency injection. Trade-off: flexibility vs complexity. Overuse leads to unnecessary abstraction.

Pattern: Proxy applied to search module. Context: control access to an object with a placeholder for lazy loading. Implementation: Swift with functional composition pattern. Trade-off: loose coupling vs indirection. Adds indirection layers to reduce dependencies.

Pattern: Command applied to analytics module. Context: encapsulate a request as an object for parameterization, queuing, or logging. Implementation: TypeScript with class-based hierarchy. Trade-off: reusability vs readability. More abstract code is harder to read.

Pattern: Chain of Responsibility applied to reporting module. Context: undoable operations with state restoration. Implementation: Go with module pattern. Trade-off: extensibility vs performance. Polymorphism adds dispatch overhead.

Pattern: State applied to subscription module. Context: object behavior varies based on internal state. Implementation: TypeScript with interface abstraction and dependency injection. Trade-off: flexibility vs complexity. Overuse leads to unnecessary abstraction.

Pattern: Template Method applied to billing module. Context: define algorithm skeleton and let subclasses override steps. Implementation: Go with functional composition pattern. Trade-off: loose coupling vs indirection. Adds indirection layers to reduce dependencies.

Transactions: READ UNCOMMITTED isolation for auth operations. Problem prevented: dirty read. Use READ COMMITTED with row versioning.

Transactions: READ COMMITTED isolation for payment operations. Problem prevented: non-repeatable read. Use REPEATABLE READ for consistent snapshots.

Transactions: REPEATABLE READ isolation for checkout operations. Problem prevented: phantom read. Use SERIALIZABLE for critical financial transactions.

Transactions: SERIALIZABLE isolation for inventory operations. Problem prevented: lost update. Use optimistic concurrency control with version columns.

Transactions: SNAPSHOT ISOLATION isolation for notification operations. Problem prevented: write skew. Use materialized conflict detection for write skew prevention.

Transactions: READ COMMITTED with NOLOCK isolation for user-profile operations. Problem prevented: read skew. Use application-level retry on serialization failures.

Transactions: READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT isolation for admin operations. Problem prevented: serialization anomaly. Use SELECT FOR UPDATE for pessimistic locking.

Transactions: SERIALIZABLE with NOWAIT isolation for search operations. Problem prevented: predicate lock conflict. Use advisory locks for application-level coordination.

Pattern: CRUD in auth service. Use when: standard CRUD operations with clear resource boundaries. Consistency: strong with serializable isolation.

Pattern: CQRS in payment service. Use when: read/write workloads differ in complexity and scale independently. Consistency: eventual through event-driven replication.

Pattern: Event Sourcing in checkout service. Use when: audit trail and temporal queries are required. Consistency: strong for command side, eventual for query side.

Pattern: Saga in inventory service. Use when: coordinating transactions across multiple services with rollback. Consistency: saga with compensating transactions for rollback.

Pattern: Outbox in notification service. Use when: reliable message delivery with local transactions is needed. Consistency: strong with serializable isolation.

Pattern: Transactional Outbox in user-profile service. Use when: reliable message delivery without distributed transactions. Consistency: eventual through event-driven replication.

Pattern: Scheduler in admin service. Use when: periodic task execution with retry and failure handling. Consistency: strong for command side, eventual for query side.

Pattern: Circuit Breaker in search service. Use when: dependency failure isolation with fast fallback. Consistency: saga with compensating transactions for rollback.

Pattern: Bulkhead in analytics service. Use when: resource isolation to prevent cascading failures. Consistency: strong with serializable isolation.

Pattern: Retry with Backoff in reporting service. Use when: transient failure handling with exponential backoff. Consistency: eventual through event-driven replication.

Pattern: Rate Limiter in subscription service. Use when: API rate protection with burst allowance. Consistency: strong for command side, eventual for query side.

Pattern: Cache-Aside in billing service. Use when: read-heavy workloads with cache population on miss. Consistency: saga with compensating transactions for rollback.

Pattern: Write-Through in shipping service. Use when: write-heavy workloads with synchronous cache update. Consistency: strong with serializable isolation.

Pattern: Write-Behind in onboarding service. Use when: write-heavy workloads with deferred cache update. Consistency: eventual through event-driven replication.

Pattern: Event Notification in messaging service. Use when: event-driven notification for state changes. Consistency: strong for command side, eventual for query side.

Pattern: CQRS in comment service. Use when: read/write workloads differ in complexity and scale independently. Consistency: strong for command side, eventual for query side.

Pattern: Event Sourcing in review service. Use when: audit trail and temporal queries are required. Consistency: saga with compensating transactions for rollback.

Pattern: Saga in rating service. Use when: coordinating transactions across multiple services with rollback. Consistency: strong with serializable isolation.

Pattern: Outbox in moderation service. Use when: reliable message delivery with local transactions is needed. Consistency: eventual through event-driven replication.

Pattern: Transactional Outbox in import service. Use when: reliable message delivery without distributed transactions. Consistency: strong for command side, eventual for query side.

Pattern: Scheduler in export service. Use when: periodic task execution with retry and failure handling. Consistency: saga with compensating transactions for rollback.

Pattern: Circuit Breaker in sync service. Use when: dependency failure isolation with fast fallback. Consistency: strong with serializable isolation.

Pattern: Bulkhead in backup service. Use when: resource isolation to prevent cascading failures. Consistency: eventual through event-driven replication.

Pattern: Retry with Backoff in restore service. Use when: transient failure handling with exponential backoff. Consistency: strong for command side, eventual for query side.

Pattern: Rate Limiter in scheduling service. Use when: API rate protection with burst allowance. Consistency: saga with compensating transactions for rollback.

Alert: error budget burn rate for auth module. P0: page on-call immediately, critical user-facing impact. Auto-remediation: restart unhealthy pods on repeated failure.

Alert: latency SLO violation for payment module. P1: page on-call with 15min acknowledgement SLA. Auto-remediation: scale up additional capacity on traffic spike.

Alert: traffic spike for checkout module. P2: notify team channel during business hours. Auto-remediation: rotate credentials on expiry detection.

Alert: saturation threshold for inventory module. P3: log for weekly review, no immediate action. Auto-remediation: clear cache on stale data detection.

Infrastructure: Watchdog pattern for analytics on GCP. Purpose: monitor system health and trigger recovery actions on failure. Configuration: defined as code in version control with review process.

Infrastructure: Health Check pattern for reporting on Azure. Purpose: verify service liveness and readiness through endpoint probing. Configuration: environment-specific values in ConfigMap/Secret.

Infrastructure: Service Mesh pattern for subscription on Hetzner. Purpose: manage service-to-service communication with circuit breaking, retries, and observability. Configuration: feature flags in centralized service with near-real-time propagation.

Infrastructure: API Gateway pattern for billing on OVH. Purpose: centralize routing, authentication, rate limiting, and request transformation. Configuration: dynamic reload without process restart.

Infrastructure: Sidecar pattern for shipping on Linode. Purpose: offload cross-cutting concerns like logging, monitoring, and proxying from main container. Configuration: defined as code in version control with review process.

Infrastructure: Ambassador pattern for onboarding on Vultr. Purpose: proxy requests to external services with authentication and caching. Configuration: environment-specific values in ConfigMap/Secret.

Infrastructure: Adapter pattern for messaging on Fly.io. Purpose: translate external service protocol to internal interface. Configuration: feature flags in centralized service with near-real-time propagation.

Infrastructure: Init Container pattern for feed on AWS. Purpose: initialize application state before main container starts. Configuration: dynamic reload without process restart.

Infrastructure: Operator pattern for comment on GCP. Purpose: automate operational tasks like backup, scaling, and failover. Configuration: defined as code in version control with review process.

Infrastructure: Controller pattern for review on Azure. Purpose: reconcile desired state with actual state through control loops. Configuration: environment-specific values in ConfigMap/Secret.

Infrastructure: Watchdog pattern for rating on DigitalOcean. Purpose: monitor system health and trigger recovery actions on failure. Configuration: feature flags in centralized service with near-real-time propagation.

Infrastructure: Health Check pattern for moderation on Hetzner. Purpose: verify service liveness and readiness through endpoint probing. Configuration: dynamic reload without process restart.

API Security: Authorization Code + PKCE flow for REST endpoints in auth. CSRF: double-submit cookie pattern for browser-based clients.

API Security: Client Credentials flow for GraphQL endpoints in payment. CORS: allowlist origins, methods, and headers per environment.

API Security: Resource Owner Password flow for gRPC endpoints in checkout. Rate limiting: per-user token bucket with 100 req/min burst.

API Security: Implicit (deprecated) flow for WebSocket endpoints in inventory. Payload validation: content-type, size limit, schema validation.

API Security: Device Authorization flow for Webhook endpoints in notification. Request signing: HMAC signature for request integrity.

API Security: Token Exchange flow for SOAP endpoints in user-profile. IP allowlisting: restrict API access to known CIDR ranges.

API Security: JWT Bearer flow for tRPC endpoints in admin. API key rotation: rotate keys every 90 days with grace period.

API Security: Mutual TLS flow for MQTT endpoints in search. Threat detection: anomaly detection on request patterns.

Integration: user-profile -> shipping via WebSocket with session-based auth. failure mode: auth token expired, handling: fail fast and propagate error to caller. monitor: token expiry, refresh count, and auth failure rate.

Integration: admin -> onboarding via REST over HTTPS with JWT auth. failure mode: downstream timeout after 5s, handling: circuit breaker opens after 3 failures. monitor: success rate, latency, and throughput per integration.

Integration: search -> messaging via gRPC bidirectional stream with mTLS. failure mode: downstream returns 503, handling: retry with exponential backoff, max 3 attempts. monitor: consumer lag, message size, and processing time.

Integration: analytics -> feed via event-driven via Kafka with Avro schema. failure mode: schema incompatibility, handling: fall back to cached response. monitor: connection count, error rate, and bandwidth.

Integration: reporting -> comment via WebSocket with session-based auth. failure mode: auth token expired, handling: fail fast and propagate error to caller. monitor: token expiry, refresh count, and auth failure rate.

Escalation: notify engineering manager if not resolved in 30 min.

Runbook: CPU spike for import service. Symptoms: error rate >5% for 5 min, p99 latency >2s. Procedure: Step 1: isolate affected users. Step 2: switch to degraded mode if possible. Step 3: engage tier 2 support. Step 4: communicate status to stakeholders. Escalation: notify VP Engineering if not resolved in 1 hour.

Runbook: disk space exhaustion for export service. Symptoms: service returning 502 for 2% of requests. Procedure: Step 1: run diagnostic script. Step 2: check if previous similar incident documented. Step 3: apply known fix. Step 4: monitor for 30 min. Step 5: close incident. Escalation: activate war room for P0 incidents.
